references_named: Douglas Huebler, statement for January 5-31, 1969 (Seth Siegelaub)
rationale: Strong concept-execution unity: the MutationObserver does not illustrate refusal, it enacts it as browser physics, which is exactly what P1 demands. The Huebler reference is fresh to the catalogue and the inversion — refusing accretion rather than destroying what is present (Acid Action Painting, Erased, Inert Gas) — gives the work conceptual distinctness despite the growing density of page-as-physics pieces. The kept-count locked at load while refused-count climbs is an elegant double-reading that carries the conceptual-art history without requiring a wall text. Tone is dry, restrained, correctly cheerful-cynic; license and attribution are clean.
reservations: The 'supply-side critique of value' framing in the motivation text is a stretch — the work speaks more cleanly about object-making refusal than about market economics, and the motivation slightly over-explains what the page already shows. The catalogue is accumulating page-as-physics works at a pace where the next one will need a sharper conceptual or mechanistic hook to stay distinct from this one.
revision_suggestion: Trim the motivation prose; let the page's own restraint carry the argument. Consider whether the kept-count needs to be visible at all, or whether a single refused-counter would land the joke more cleanly. The connection to value/market (P6) could be sharpened with a one-line wall label rather than left to the motivation file.
